taxpayer.filing_status_claimed: none (no return filed; SFR under sec. 6020(b)); head of household conceded
taxpayer.notes: Separated from spouse in May 2017 and maintained separate households thereafter; wife not a party. Operated Surplus & Adventure, Fibre Arts, and STEAM Works; co-owned Beavercreek, Ohio and Lexington Park, Maryland real estate with wife.

adjustments: standard deduction $6,350 and one personal exemption $3,888 allowed
tax of $660 on IRAs, other retirement plans, and MSAs (computational)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Deficiency; asserted business, rental, car/truck, meals and depreciation deductions after petition; 6651(a)(1) addition
conceded: Petitioner not liable for sec. 6651(a)(2) addition
Petitioner not liable for sec. 6654 addition
Petitioner entitled to head of household filing status
Petitioner entitled to three personal exemptions
Surplus & Adventure gross receipts $10,404; cost of goods sold $7,595
Fibre Arts gross receipts $3,238; cost of goods sold $7,595 (as listed in the table)
Maryland rental property net rental income $18,948.50; real estate taxes $2,887.33; mortgage interest $8,917.28; hazard insurance $845.48
Oakwood residence used as personal residence in 2017; real estate taxes $13,560.03 and mortgage interest $9,264.48 (petitioner sole payor/borrower)
Respondent conceded at trial that Beavercreek property was rented as a business for five months of 2017

findings_of_fact.fact: Surplus & Adventure substantiated expenses: advertising/marketing $1,092.37, PayPal fees $1,077.77, Penske truck rental $80.19, FedEx/USPS shipping $229.94
findings_of_fact.snippet: petitioner paid advertising/marketing expenses of $ 1,092.37, PayPal fees of $1,077.77, a Penske truck rental expense of $80.19, and shipping fees

findings_of_fact.fact: Fibre Arts substantiated expenses: Etsy selling fees $202.90 and Ohio business filing fees $145.15
findings_of_fact.snippet: petitioner paid Etsy selling fees of $202.90 and Ohio business filing fees of $145.15.

findings_of_fact.fact: Car and truck expense records were noncontemporaneous mileage estimates lacking dates and business purpose
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner did not keep contemporaneous records of the amount of each separate expense, but rather noncontemporaneous estimates of mileage driven for his business.

findings_of_fact.fact: STEAM Works had no gross receipts in 2017 and was operated as a hobby without profit objective
findings_of_fact.snippet: STEAM Works did not have any gross receipts in 2017.

findings_of_fact.fact: Beavercreek property: petitioner and wife jointly paid real estate taxes $4,715.32 and mortgage interest $5,490.90; petitioner paid one half
findings_of_fact.snippet: During 2017 petitioner and his wife jointly paid real estate taxes and mortgage interest of $4,715.32 and $5,490.90, respectively, for the Beavercreek property.

findings_of_fact.fact: Beavercreek property rented five months; not rented or personal residence the other seven months
findings_of_fact.snippet: In 2017 petitioner rented out the Beavercreek property for five months out of the year.

findings_of_fact.fact: Beavercreek owner activity statement expenses totaled $1,199.36, paid by petitioner; only petitioner received rental income
findings_of_fact.snippet: an owner activity statement listing the 2017 expenses, totaling $1,199.36. The parties have stipulated that petitioner paid those expenses.

findings_of_fact.fact: Maryland property: jointly paid real estate taxes $2,887.33 and mortgage interest $8,917.28; petitioner paid one half; rented all of 2017
findings_of_fact.snippet: During 2017 petitioner and his wife jointly paid real estate taxes and mortgage interest of $2,887.33 and $8,917.28, respectively, for the Maryland property.

findings_of_fact.fact: Maryland property: Form 1099-MISC gross income $21,000; net rental income $18,948.50; petitioner paid property expenses $2,051.50 and hazard insurance $845.48; deductible total $2,896.98
findings_of_fact.snippet: petitioner may deduct those expenses totaling $2,896.98 under sections 162(a) and 212(2).

findings_of_fact.fact: Meals records lacked business purpose; depreciation claims lacked basis, useful life, prior depreciation
findings_of_fact.snippet: none of his records included a referenced business purpose for his asserted meals expenses.

findings_of_fact.fact: Extension to October 15, 2018 obtained; no return filed by extended due date; IRS prepared SFR under sec. 6020(b)
findings_of_fact.snippet: required to be filed by October 15, 2018, and petitioner did not file his return by that date.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner did not show reasonable cause; argued only that he owed no deficiency
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner has not shown reasonable cause for failing to timely file his 2017 tax return.

issues.question: Other (sec. 162 business expenses, Schedule C): Which asserted 2017 Surplus & Adventure expenses (including car/truck and depreciation) are deductible?
issues.holding: Deductible: advertising $1,092.37, PayPal fees $1,077.77, truck rental $80.19, shipping $229.94; car/truck expenses fail strict substantiation; depreciation not substantiated

amount_determined.description: allowed Surplus & Adventure expenses (sum not stated)

issues.computable_reason: Turns on substantiation of expenses; allowed amounts are found facts, not statutory computation

issues.question: Other (sec. 162 business expenses): Which asserted 2017 Fibre Arts expenses (including car/truck and depreciation) are deductible?
issues.holding: Deductible: Etsy fees $202.90 and Ohio filing fees $145.15; car/truck and depreciation (embroidery machines, generator, trailer) disallowed

issues.question: Other (sec. 183 hobby loss): Was STEAM Works engaged in for profit, and are its expenses deductible?
issues.holding: Not engaged in for profit (hobby); with zero gross income, no expenses deductible under sec. 183(b)
issues.computable_reason: Profit-objective finding is a nine-factor facts-and-circumstances judgment; once hobby status found, the sec. 183(b) limit to $0 gross income is mechanical

issues.question: Other (secs. 162/212/163(h)/164 rental property): What deductions are allowed for the Beavercreek property for 2017?
issues.holding: Petitioner may deduct 5/12 of his half of mortgage interest and real estate taxes under secs. 162(a)/212(2) and the remaining 7/12 as itemized deductions under secs. 163(h)/164(a); 5/12 of the $1,199.36 owner-statement expenses deductible, 7/12 personal; car/truck, meals, depreciation disallowed

amount_determined.description: allocations stated as fractions; dollar amounts not stated

issues.computable_reason: Given found amounts, ownership share (1/2) and months rented (5 of 12), the allocation is arithmetic; disallowed items rest on substantiation

issues.question: Other (secs. 162/212 rental property): What deductions are allowed for the Maryland property for 2017?
issues.holding: Petitioner may deduct one half of real estate taxes ($2,887.33) and mortgage interest ($8,917.28), plus expenses of $2,051.50 and hazard insurance $845.48 totaling $2,896.98; car/truck, meals, depreciation (house, fence) disallowed
issues.computable_reason: Half-share of stipulated amounts and stipulated expenses is arithmetic; disallowed items rest on substantiation

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the sec. 6651(a)(1) addition to tax for failure to timely file his 2017 return?
issues.holding: Liable to the extent there is a deficiency after Rule 155 computations; no return filed by extended due date; SFR is not a taxpayer return; no reasonable cause shown

amount_determined.description: addition determined in notice (to be recomputed under Rule 155)

issues.computable_reason: No return ever filed and no reasonable cause asserted; amount is 5% per month up to 25% of the net amount due after Rule 155 recomputation

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Some substantiated business and rental expenses allowed (rental allocations by ownership share and months rented); car/truck, meals, depreciation and STEAM Works hobby expenses disallowed; 6651(a)(1) addition sustained; 6651(a)(2) and 6654 conceded by respondent

notes: Many items stipulated/conceded (table on pp. 2-3). Fibre Arts COGS listed as $7,595 in the concession table, identical to Surplus & Adventure COGS (as printed). Burden on petitioner (sec. 7491(a) not shown). Derived: Beavercreek petitioner half-share = $2,357.66 taxes and $2,745.45 interest; Maryland half-share = $1,443.665 taxes and $4,458.64 interest (not stated by court). Sec. 280A not applied to Beavercreek (fn. 5).
